holidays.name: National Bittersweet Chocolate with Almonds Day
holidays.description: This is a day for people who like their chocolate dark, a little grown-up, and crunchy. Snap off a piece of bittersweet chocolate studded with toasted almonds. Let the bitter and the nutty flavors mix. Some people call it a candy bar with a graduate degree.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance, and its origin is unclear. It has appeared on fun-holiday calendars for years as a tribute to one of the great chocolate pairings.
holidays.funFact: Almonds aren't true nuts. They are the seeds of a fruit related to peaches and cherries, so this treat is technically chocolate with fruit pits.

holidays.name: Hug a Bear Day
holidays.description: Today is for celebrating bears of every kind. That includes teddy bears, gummy bears, and, from a respectful distance, the real ones. Squeeze your oldest stuffed bear, and leave the grizzlies alone.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It is a playful nod to the teddy bear, which was named after President Theodore "Teddy" Roosevelt after a famous 1902 hunting trip.
holidays.funFact: The first teddy bears appeared in toy shops soon after Roosevelt's 1902 Mississippi hunting trip. He had refused to shoot a captured bear, and a cartoon of the moment inspired the toy.
